name: Baroque Mythological Sky
description: Gods and heroes carried on banks of cloud in the high-baroque manner — long diagonal compositions, drapery billowing in crimson, gold and slate, cherubs at the edges, an eagle or a trident or a lyre held plainly, and warm flesh lit against a stormy or gilded sky, painted as oil on canvas or as fresco.
style_bible: High-baroque figure painting of the seventeenth century, in the manner of Rubens and of Giulio Romano's ceiling decoration — worked as oil on a coarse primed canvas or as fresco on lime plaster, always painted and never photographed. Ground and surface: the canvas weave or the plaster tooth shows through the thinner darks, the paint is laid warm over a russet ground, flesh is built in soft blended half-tones with a loaded impasto only on the brightest turn of a shoulder or a knee, and the whole surface carries a fine craquelure under a warm varnish bloom. Composition: everything moves on a long diagonal. Figures are arranged in a rising or falling sweep from one lower corner toward the opposite upper corner, foreshortened as though seen from below, with limbs and drapery crossing the diagonal to hold the eye inside the frame; nothing is centred, nothing is symmetrical, and no figure stands square to the viewer. Cloud: the ground the figures rest on is cloud itself — dense sunlit banks piled like carded wool at the top, dissolving into slate and violet shadow beneath, thick enough to bear weight where a body touches it and thin enough at the edges to let a limb pass through. Drapery: cloth is a character. Great lengths of it billow and snap around the figures in deep crimson, in gold and ochre, and in cool slate, falling in heavy sculptural folds with a broad lit face, a deep shadow trough and a warm reflected light at the return; it is never still and never neatly arranged. Palette: warm flesh tones — cream, rose and umber — carried against a sky that is either stormy in slate, bruised violet and grey-green, or gilded in amber, honey and pale gold. Crimson and gold are the only fully saturated notes; the darks are warm browns rather than black, and the whites are linen and cloud rather than paper. Light: strong chiaroscuro from a single high source outside the frame, so one side of every figure is fully lit and the other falls into a warm shadow that keeps its colour; a shaft or opening of brighter sky sits behind the principal figure, and the darkest mass of the picture is placed against it. Figures and attendants: adult gods and heroes are built heavy and physical, muscular and softly fleshed rather than lean, and small winged cherubs cluster at the edges of the group, tumbling, carrying and reaching, always subordinate and never the subject. Attributes: each figure holds or is accompanied by one plainly readable attribute — an eagle, a peacock, a trident, a lyre, a caduceus, a bow, a wheat sheaf, a hammer, a chalice, a serpent, a torch, a helm — placed so it is legible at small size and drawn as a real object rather than as a symbol floating free. Mood: elevated, weightless, unhurried, and calm even in motion; this look is used for long quiet narration, so the drama sits in the composition and the light rather than in a face. Keep the contract content-independent: no named deity, no fixed episode, no insignia, no wordmark and no copied composition.
